properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 11 at 12:12AM CST by NWS Wichita KS
properties.description:
Optimal radiational cooling and ample moisture are supporting
another morning of fog across the area. However, a frontal
boundary is quickly progressing southward across Kansas, and
increasing winds in association with this frontal boundary will
lead to the dissipation of any fog that develops early this
morning. However, prior to the front's arrival, patchy dense fog
appears likely with a couple of spotters across south-central
Kansas already reporting visibility under one quarter mile in some
locations. If traveling early this morning, slow down and use
extra caution in areas of reduced visibility.

properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics earlier today has mostly ended, but
flooding on the Skokomish River will continue into Wednesday the the
flood crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Tuesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Tuesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river will crest around 17.5 feet later tonight.
It will then fall below flood stage around midday Wednesday.
Another return to flood stage is possible late this week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 715 AM PST.

this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. There is
potential for advisory-level surf, enhanced beach erosion and
minor tidal overflows. Posing most risk to west-facing
beaches. Coastal hazards are likely to continue well into next
week.

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 7:48PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. Water levels
continue to slowly rise at upstream gauges. The river is forecast to
remain within Major flood stage through this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Tuesday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, cresting at
17.2 feet this weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

weather pattern.

until conditions improve.
